clue.text: Feat hiding double-D with one fan!

indicators.note: something hiding another thing keeps it tucked inside itself, so one word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a feat is a deed or act
two Ds
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a large bra size and the admirer it attracts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-D' looks like a bra cup size, but it simply supplies two Ds to go with the one.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a devotee or enthusiast, as in a jazz addict, so it can stand for a keen fan.

clue.text: Yobbo standing on testicle presents a real problem

blocks.note: a tough is a rough, violent young man
nut is slang for a testicle

explanation.surface: A thug standing on someone's privates creates genuine trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'standing on' puts the first piece on top of the second. A yobbo is a British word for a loutish youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough nut, as in a tough nut to crack, is a difficult problem or person hard to deal with.

clue.text: (+ 17ac.) Shoot up in Milan, possibly taking an E

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter itself, though the surface reads it as ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone injecting drugs in an Italian city while also taking an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E' looks like street slang for an ecstasy tablet, but it is simply the letter added to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To mainline is slang for injecting a drug straight into a vein, which is what shooting up means.

clue.text: Will the pretentious columnist take heroine from the rack?

definitions.note: the surname of the writer Will Self

indicators.note: to take something from a place removes it, so a letter is lifted out of the word

blocks.note: a rack for storing things
H is slang for heroin; the extra E disguises the drug as a female hero

explanation.surface: Asks whether a writer will snort a drug off a shelf, suggesting a drug-using journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Self is an English novelist and columnist known for his elaborate vocabulary and admitted heroin use, hence the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Self is the British writer and columnist often mocked for pretentious prose, so his surname is clued by naming him.

clue.text: No other sort of sex makes car steamy?

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile
steamy can mean sexually charged

explanation.surface: Suggests some odd kind of sex that fogs up a car's windows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: sex with no other person involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Autoerotic describes sexual activity performed on oneself alone, with no partner taking part.

clue.text: Roman backstabber needs to be in a state of sexual excitement in number 10, possibly

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: a bus has a route number, such as the number 10
rut is the mating season frenzy of male deer

explanation.surface: Suggests a treacherous politician getting aroused inside Number 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' looks like the Prime Minister's residence at 10 Downing Street, but it is a bus route.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was among the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, so he is history's archetypal treacherous friend.

clue.text: (see 10ac.)
Defender of a nasty video one put out about "pussy"

indicators.note: something put out has been ejected, so a letter is thrown out of the word
something nasty is spoiled or disordered, so the remaining letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round another word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, the letter removed
pussy is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lawyer defending a smutty video that someone released.
explanation.walkthrough: The scare quotes on 'pussy' tempt a ruder reading, but it is just the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is someone who pleads a case, such as a barrister, so a defender in court.

clue.text: "Getting a hard-on right" row leads to pandemonium

blocks.note: a crude way of saying getting it up
R is the standard abbreviation for right
to row is to use an oar, and oar is also a verb meaning to row

explanation.surface: An argument about arousal descends into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel sitting comfortably with pandemonium, but here it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud, chaotic disturbance, which is exactly what pandemonium means.

clue.text: (& 7dn./16) Religiously staying in tune with the party line?

annotation.answer: SINGING FROM THE SAME HYMN SHEET

definitions.text: Religiously staying in tune with the party line?

blocks.note: the surface: a church congregation keeping in tune together
the setter's reading: politicians all repeating the same agreed message

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is political jargon for party members all giving the same message, pictured literally as a choir in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means presenting a united front and agreeing on what to say, as party loyalists must.

clue.text: On a trip, Stephen was so done in

blocks.note: first meaning: high on drugs
second meaning: St Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was killed by having rocks thrown at him

explanation.surface: Someone named Stephen on holiday gets exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' suggests a journey and 'done in' tiredness; the clue means a drug trip and a martyr's execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated by drugs, and also describes the biblical death of Saint Stephen by stoning.

clue.text: Following her ex-daughter-in-law's allegation, Brenda in denial

blocks.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, was the Queen's former daughter-in-law; her name shortens to Di
an allegation is a claim
Private Eye nicknames the Queen Brenda; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen refusing to accept what Princess Diana had alleged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the Queen's letters after the rest. Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a statement renouncing responsibility or connection, which is a formal denial.

clue.text: Bob screwed by heartless Tory curse

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle of the word is removed and only its ends are kept
screwed up means twisted and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the outside letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Bob has been cheated by a cruel Conservative's hex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is a quick bending of the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a small quick curtsey, the bending of the knees as a mark of respect.

clue.text: Inside city limits act like one with a chopper that's soft and sticky

indicators.note: a word's limits are its boundaries, so only its first and last letters are kept
inside puts one piece within the other

blocks.note: the outer letters of the word

blocks.clueFragment: act like one with a chopper
blocks.note: to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone wielding an axe within the city boundary, oddly described as soft and sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: A chopper suggests a helicopter or slang for a penis, but here it is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy food, such as toffee, is soft and sticky and needs plenty of chewing.

clue.text: Tart from US city, getting end away, rejected

indicators.note: with its end taken away the word loses its final letter; the phrase is also slang for having sex
something rejected is sent back, so the word is read from the other direction

blocks.note: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma

explanation.surface: A promiscuous American woman has sex and is then cast off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply strips the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart and slut are both derogatory slang words for a promiscuous woman, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Parliamentarian malarky settled when we replaced Tony finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name
one thing replaced another means it takes the other's place, so letters are swapped
something settled has been sorted into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, swapped in
the last letter of the name, swapped out

explanation.surface: A politician's nonsense calmed down once Tony Blair was gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony is Tony Blair, a frequent target of Private Eye; only his last letter is used, and WE takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentarian is a member of a legislature, someone who makes the laws, so a lawmaker.

clue.text: (see 10ac.)
(see 3dn.)
Didn't put away all the chicken Labour traditionalists Tony distances himself from?

definitions.text: Didn't put away all the chicken
Labour traditionalists Tony distances himself from

blocks.clueFragment: Didn't put away all the chicken
blocks.note: first meaning: leaving part of a chicken, a limb, uneaten

blocks.clueFragment: Labour traditionalists Tony distances himself from
blocks.note: second meaning: the socialist faction of the Labour Party that Tony Blair's New Labour sidelined

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a past-tense phrase, left plus wing, about an unfinished meal; the second is the political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: The left wing of the Labour Party holds its traditional socialist views, which Blair's New Labour moved away from.

clue.text: Mel's involved with Tony's ultimate web site undergoing seemingly endless reconstruction

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter of the name is used
involved means tangled and intricate, so the letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Suggests a celebrity and Tony Blair are linked to a website stuck in permanent redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley Stadium in London was rebuilt between 2003 and 2007 after long delays, which the definition mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The national football stadium at Wembley, north London, had a notoriously long and overrunning rebuild.

clue.text: Married and put in order? Rubbish!

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
to align is to put things in a line or order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of getting married and sorting their life out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' reads as a scornful exclamation, but it is a verb meaning to disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish someone is British slang for running them down, which is to malign or speak badly of them.

clue.text: Eff-off when collared by Olympic Games campaigner – Columbian?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged
a collar goes round the neck, so being collared means being enclosed by another word

blocks.note: the spelling of the letter F
Sebastian Coe led London's bid for the 2012 Olympics

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal is shouted at Seb Coe's Olympic campaign, apparently from someone from Colombia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: Colombia, spelt Columbian here, is famous for its coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombian is a well-known variety of coffee, so the question mark marks it as one example of the drink.

clue.text: Bevin's grave is lacking one

definitions.note: the first name of the Labour politician Ernest Bevin

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: grave and earnest both mean serious
a means one, as in a book

explanation.surface: Someone's burial place is missing a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place, but it is an adjective meaning serious. Ernest Bevin was a Labour foreign secretary after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Bevin, the trade unionist and post-war Foreign Secretary, had Ernest as his first name, so it is Bevin's.

clue.text: Like the typical bombastic politician wants every known beer plus roll

blocks.note: every and all both cover the whole
piss is a rude slang name for weak beer
and adds one thing to another
to wind and to roll both mean to coil up

explanation.surface: A politician demands every beer going and a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like bread to go with the beer, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all piss and wind is full of empty boasting and talk, typical of a bombastic politician.

clue.text: (+24) Decline podium occupied by flipping Brown

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the word is written backwards
a place occupied by something holds it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: a podium is a raised stage
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown clings to the lectern while his fortunes fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping Brown' reads like an exasperated curse at the Prime Minister Gordon Brown, but it turns a colour backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop developing and fall into decline, like still water going stale.

clue.text: (see 23)
Darwin's transport for the heavy smoker?

blocks.note: first meaning: HMS ..., the ship on which Charles Darwin sailed round the world
second meaning: the dog breed notoriously used to test cigarettes in laboratory experiments

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is grimly comic: beagles were forced to inhale tobacco smoke in laboratory research.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle carried Darwin on his voyage, and the beagle dog was the standard subject of tobacco experiments.

clue.text: Like scattering shit on floor

blocks.note: the surface: a filthy mess spread across a room
the setter's reading: the quality of conceptual installations that pass off mess as art

explanation.walkthrough: The clue mocks modern conceptual art, where a scattered mess in a gallery can be passed off as a serious work.
explanation.definitionFit: Artiness is a pretentious display of artistic qualities, which is how the setter sees such installations.
